svg.title: The inverse and norm here are on the full tensor coordinate space, including its scalar directions. The norm of eBk is exactly ∥T 0∥, so finite-dimensional compactness gives a convergent subsequence with limit B of that norm. No positive lower bound on ξk is needed. Closedness of the real signed symmetric space puts B in that space. Its free mean is zero: the one-point comparison for bounded converging labels applies to eBk, while its physical image is the positive scalar multiple ξ−1 k r4 kJ, whose expectation is exactly zero. Applying the converging derivative matrices (WS7) to eBk similarly passes the exact physical divergence zero to the free divergence zero. Thus B ∈ker D0. By its one-dimensionality, B = cT 0 for real c; equality of norms gives |c| = 1. Choose the single sign of J that makes c = 1. Restricting the comparison parameter to this subsequence preserves all earlier limits and exact compatibility laws. This proves the normalized stress comparison used above; its eventual Ward amplitude is fixed separately below.
